items.id: ENV-1 RIFT canopy: 2nd and 3rd crown species
items.evidence: Code exists: terrain.ts treeVariantOf (grove cells, west/east shares blended across the middle third, a fifth of species groves stay Dialwood), map_rift.json props.tree gains hourtier.glb / lampbough.glb plus art.terrain.treeGroves, dialwood.py builds them. Re-ran _harness/max2_env_treecount.mjs: 1982 trees, 1,198,424 tris = 604.6 per tree (Hourtier 600, Lampbough 528), so the -2.5 % claim holds. Crops of max2_after4/rift_jungle_s and rift_jungle_e: the Hourtier reads as stacked silvered-sage tiers and the Lampbough as a spiky rust parasol, so the wood now reads as three species at the game camera. This closes critic gap 6's main item. Spot counts are triangle-neutral (jungle_e 195k -> 187k, core 131k -> 134k), with +2 to 6 draws and programs still 39.

terrain_glsl.ts WALL_MAIN kind 6, the Dialwood block-top only (uStoneTop 0, RIFT): dapple, species drifts, dial-stone slabs with seams. On ENV-1_floor_breakup_ab.png the gain is modest. The slabs show as faint paler patches and the dapple pools barely read. It is no longer one even moss, but it is still a dark floor.

The cool-grey chunks are gone. The chunks now read dark umber, close to near-black in shade (max2c_struct_ruin.png), so see problems.

ENV-6_soot_fix_ab.png: visible at stages 1 and 2 and on the ruin, but it reads mostly as an overall warm-brown darkening of the shell. Distinct patches and streaks are hard to see at the game camera.

terrain_glsl.ts GROUND_MAIN plaza block: per-flag families, one flag in eleven darker, a walked track toward the map middle, kerb drift. Floor only, with no change to tris or draws in bridge_base or rift_core. ENV-5_plaza_dressing_ab.png: the per-flag variation is faintly visible. It is subtle, as the engineer says, and value_probe plaza saturation stays 0.32 / 0.36-0.37 PASS.

terrain_glsl.ts VALE_STYLE_SPAN deck-bay block exists (9 m bays, ±4.5 % tone via 0.09*(hash-0.5), chalk ticks, joints x0.66). On ENV-11_deck_bays_ab.png at the gameplay camera only one or two faint cross lines are visible, and the chalk hour ticks cannot be seen. The deck still reads as one even run of courses.

ENV-7_slab_recapture.png on the current build: the shadow-slab hour band still reads, and the round-2 start and now frames are identical, as claimed (no code change). Closes critic weakAB 6's request for a recapture.
The decision is recorded in summary.json, and the reason (top-down smear, overdraw, a 41st program against 40/40) is sound against the live counts I measured.

Since round-1 ship 36163c40b the lane's diff touches only terrain.ts, terrain_glsl.ts, structures.ts, map_rift.json, dialwood.py/scatter.py and two tree GLBs. The post, fog, quality, sky, ink and ambient files are unchanged. actors.ts and director.ts changes belong to the units and vfx lanes. The block-top break-up is RIFT-only (FRAY's kind 6 takes the uStoneTop branch, BRIDGE's gorge takes uStoneTop 2). FRAY spot counts are unchanged (132k/94/30, 35k/66/30).

problems.what: The 500k match triangle margin is down to about 5k: seed 11 peaks at 495k (my run), against 462k at the round-1 idle gate.
problems.evidence: My perf_1080 --prod --match-only --match-seeds 7,11,23: seed 11 peak frame actors 320k / canopy 29k / vfx 28k. The canopy is 2.5 % lighter per tree, so the rise is not this lane's. It still passes, but any lane adding a triangle now risks the gate.
problems.fix: Lead: actor triangle growth (units/fighter rebuilds) must pay back before the final idle gate; env must stay neutral or negative.

problems.what: The BRIDGE deck bays do not read at the gameplay camera. ENV-11 is in the code but is effectively invisible.
problems.evidence: ENV-11_deck_bays_ab.png: bridge_deck shows one or two faint cross lines, and the chalk ticks are not visible. bridge_snap is indistinguishable from before.
problems.fix: Raise the drum course's value step and its joint contrast within the lane's value band (keep laneP50 85-100, walkableSpread <= 45), or widen the course. Keep it hue-led so telegraphs stay on top.

problems.what: Soot reads as an overall warm-brown tint on the damaged tower and ruin, not as patches and streaks; the rubble chunks and the ruin are now dark umber, near-black in shade.
problems.evidence: ENV-6_soot_fix_ab.png (stage 1 and 2 shells go evenly darker brown), ENV-6_rubble_fix_ab.png and max2c_struct_ruin.png (chunks sit at the bottom of the value range under the wall's shadow). Round-1 verify2 counted 'none near black' as a gain.
problems.fix: Lower the global grime multiplier (0.88/0.8/0.7 at uSoot 1.2) so the patch mask carries the read, and give the rubble's soot (0.75) a lighter floor so the chunks keep about L* 20+ in shade.

problems.what: The Lampbough reads rust red-brown, not the 'amber' the claim and comments name, and in a grove it looks like an autumn maple.
problems.evidence: max2_after4/rift_jungle_e.png: 6.7 % of the frame is saturated hue < 28 deg (red-brown); only 0.09 % falls in the reserved harm band 28-50 deg, so ruling 32's reserved hue is not hit. The colour is VALE's own but generic.
problems.fix: Optional: push the Lampbough toward its named amber (hue about 30-35 deg) at lower saturation, keeping it out of the harm band by saturation (<= 40 %), or lean into the quill silhouette.

problems.what: Stale shader comments do not match the code.
problems.evidence: terrain_glsl.ts deck bays: the comment says ±2.5 %, the code is ±4.5 %. Plaza: the comment says ±3 %, the code spans 0.95-1.03 plus the 0.86 replacement flags, so the plaza mean drops about 2 % rather than being held.
problems.fix: Update the comments (or the code) so the tokens and comments stay the law.

budgets: Re-measured on a fresh npm run -s build, through the heavy queue. perf_1080 --prod --match-only --match-seeds 7,11,23: GATE PASS. Peaks 454k / 495k / 459k tris, 287 / 272 / 287 draws, 40 programs, 0 programs first seen after 1:00. Frame timing is not claimed (load 20-370). value_probe tag v1renv, rift/bridge/fray x high/low: 0 FAIL. Structure L* p95 RIFT 77.5 high / 79.5 low, BRIDGE 75 / 76.5, all <= 80, which matches the engineer. Frame p99 115-141 (<= 180), env p99 103-119 (<= 160), RIFT and FRAY High walkableSpread 44 of 45. typecheck exit 0. content:check OK, 0 warnings. probe: 54 of 55 PASS. The one FAIL is probe_sim_core_nav 'grid A* cross-wall search cost' at 3.8-4.6 ms against a 3 ms wall-clock bar under load 20-60. src/sim has no change since round 1 and the lane's map_rift.json change is art.terrain only, so this is load, not the lane. The first full run also hit my 900 s outer timeout at load 373, and I re-ran the remaining sim probes. The treecount script confirms 604.6 tris per tree. probe_match_memory was not re-run: the lane adds two tree GLBs (22.7 + 19.6 KB), two instanced geometries and a few material clones per ruin, which is negligible against the 2865/3000 MB RIFT margin. The idle reading is owed to the final gate, as the engineer says.
notes: Every claim exists in code and content as described. No blocker or major, no sensitivity issue (trees, floor and stone only; no faces or hoods). Originality: the Hourtier tiers and Lampbough quill parasol are VALE's own and have no LoL counterpart. Regression lens: nothing broken; programs held at 40 through the rubble and ruin material clones; FRAY untouched; B5 kept. Against round 1 (7.4) the lane is clearly better: the RIFT wood finally reads as three species, the outflow fall reads, the rubble and soot states exist. The plaza, deck bays and floor break-up are subtle to near-invisible, so the score sits just over par at 7.6.
